fr.elements: Main Residence; Vehicle Parking Area; Access Drive; Detached Structure; Dense Vegetation; Open Lawn Area; Walkway
fr.considerations: Multiple Access Points; Dense Vegetation; Limited Visibility
fr.recommendations:
• Install reflective address numbers visible from the road at the driveway entrance to help responders locate the property quickly at night or in low visibility.
• Mark the access drive entrance with reflective driveway markers so responders can identify the turn-in from the road.
• Trim vegetation along the sides of the access drive to maintain a clear path wide enough for emergency vehicles.
• Cut back dense vegetation that blocks sightlines at the access drive entrance so responders can safely enter and exit without blind-spot conflicts.
• Keep the vehicle parking area clear of parked vehicles or equipment that could block emergency vehicle access or turnaround.
• Mark any secondary access points with visible signage so responders arriving from different directions can quickly identify all available entry routes.
• Keep a clear path along the walkway between the main residence and the detached structure so responders can move between buildings on foot without obstruction.
• Thin dense vegetation between the main residence and detached structure so responders can see and reach both buildings from a staging position.
• Keep the open lawn area free of stored materials, equipment, or debris so it remains available as a responder staging area.
• If the detached structure has its own access point, mark it clearly and keep it unlocked or provide key access information to your local fire department.

wildfire.conditions: Tree Cluster; Large Trees; Scattered Trees; Vegetation Near Structure; Vegetation Near Structure; Open Terrain; Multiple Access Routes; Adequate Vegetation Separation
wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim branches from large trees that extend directly over or toward the structures.
• Thin the tree cluster to create more open space between individual trees and reduce the chance of fire moving tree to tree.
• Remove shrubs and low-growing plants that are directly touching or within a few feet of any structure.
• Separate scattered trees from nearby structures by trimming lower limbs up from the ground.
• Keep the area beneath large trees clear of dead leaves, fallen branches, and dry plant debris.
• Maintain the open terrain areas by keeping them free of accumulating dead grass, brush, or debris piles.
• Keep all access routes clear of overhanging branches and encroaching vegetation so vehicles can pass through without obstruction.
